s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest and back pain with progressive dyspnea and electrocardiogram changes
salient_findings: Persistent chest and back pain
Dyspnea on exertion
Diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR
Elevated cardiac troponin I level
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle
Cystic mass above the left atrium
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
History of hypertension
Chest discomfort and dyspnea on exertion for two months
Sinus rhythm with diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR
Occasional premature ventricular complexes
Elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Cystic mass above the left atrium on contrast-enhanced CT scan
Mass had heterogeneous attenuation on noncontrast images
Mass exhibited slight contrast enhancement
Transient cardiogenic shock after CT scan
Responded to noradrenaline support

shortlist.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and electrocardiogram changes

shortlist.label: Cardiac Tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium and transient cardiogenic shock

shortlist.label: Myocardial Infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest discomfort and electrocardiogram changes with ST elevation in lead aVR

shortlist.label: Cardiac Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and contrast enhancement

raw.rationale: The presence of a large cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and slight contrast enhancement, along with the patient's symptoms and cardiac findings, suggests a cardiac tumor such as cardiac sarcoma, which can cause cardiac dysfunction and obstructive symptoms.

rejected.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated troponin and ST-segment changes, the presence of a large cystic mass is not typical for acute coronary syndrome

rejected.label: Cardiac Tamponade
rejected.why: There is no mention of a significant pericardial effusion, which is a hallmark of cardiac tamponade

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings are not typical for a straightforward myocardial infarction, and the presence of a mass suggests another underlying cause

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging findings do not suggest pericarditis, which typically presents with pericardial effusion and/or thickening
